notesEn.usage: Connects two independent clauses to show sequential order ('A and then B') or simple addition ('A and B').
notesEn.nuance: Directly attaches to the stem without needing stem vowel changes.

notesId.usage: Menghubungkan dua klausa independen untuk menunjukkan urutan ('A lalu B') atau penambahan sederhana ('A dan B').
notesId.nuance: Langsung ditempelkan pada kata dasar tanpa memerlukan perubahan vokal.

examples.meaningEn: I ate a meal and drank coffee.
This book is interesting and cheap.
I will do homework and then sleep.
examples.meaningId: Saya akan mengerjakan PR lalu tidur.

quiz.question: Which connector means 'and' when joining two action clauses?
quiz.explanationEn: ~고 joins two clauses sequentially or additively.
quiz.explanationId: ~고 menghubungkan dua klausa secara berurutan atau sebagai penambahan.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I ate a meal and drank coffee. -> 밥을 먹___ 커피를 마셨어요.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I ate a meal and drank coffee.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya makan dan minum kopi.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use meal (밥을) + eat (먹) + connective (고) + coffee (커피를) + drank (마셨어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan nasi/makanan (밥을) + makan (먹) + penghubung (고) + kopi (커피를) + minum lampau (마셨어요).

notesEn.nuance: Directly attaches to present or past stems regardless of final consonant or vowel.

notesId.nuance: Langsung ditempelkan pada kata dasar masa kini atau masa lalu tanpa memandang konsonan atau vokal akhir.

examples.meaningEn: Korean is difficult, but it is fun.
It is cheap, but the quality is good.

examples.meaningId: Hujan turun, tetapi saya tetap pergi.

quiz.question: Which suffix is used to connect two contrasting facts ('A, but B')?
quiz.explanationEn: ~지만 is the direct contrast connective suffix equivalent to 'but'.
quiz.explanationId: ~지만 adalah akhiran penghubung kontras langsung yang setara dengan 'tetapi'.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Korean is difficult, but it is fun. -> 한국어는 어렵___ 재미있어요.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Korean is difficult, but it is fun.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Bahasa Korea sulit, tetapi seru.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use Korean (한국어는) + difficult stem (어렵) + but (지만) + fun (재미있어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan bahasa Korea (한국어는) + kata dasar sulit (어렵) + tetapi (지만) + seru (재미있어요).

meaningEn: Sequential cause and effect connection ('so / because').

notesEn.formation: Stem with ㅏ/ㅗ -> ~아서. Other vowels -> ~어서. Stem ending in 하다 -> ~해서.
notesEn.usage: Connects a cause or condition in the first clause to its logical result in the second.
notesEn.nuance: Cannot be used with imperative or propositional sentence endings (use ~(으)니까 instead).

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar bervokal ㅏ/ㅗ -> ~아서. Vokal lain -> ~어서. Kata Dasar berakhiran 하다 -> ~해서.
notesId.usage: Menghubungkan sebab atau kondisi pada klausa pertama ke hasil logisnya pada klausa kedua.
notesId.nuance: Tidak dapat digunakan dengan kalimat perintah atau ajakan (gunakan ~(으)니까 sebagai gantinya).

examples.meaningEn: It rained, so I stayed home.
examples.meaningId: Karena hujan, saya ada di rumah.

examples.meaningEn: I was tired, so I slept early.
examples.meaningId: Karena lelah, saya tidur lebih awal.

examples.meaningEn: I was hungry, so I ate a meal.

quiz.question: What is the correct causal form of '피곤하다' (to be tired)?
quiz.explanationEn: Verbs/Adjectives ending in 하다 always change to 해서 for this pattern.
quiz.explanationId: Kata kerja/sifat yang berakhiran 하다 selalu berubah menjadi 해서 untuk pola ini.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: It rained, so I stayed home. -> 비가 오___ 집에 있었어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 오 contains the vowel ㅗ, so merge it into 와서 (오 + 아서).
fillInTheBlank.hintId: 오 mengandung vokal ㅗ, jadi leburkan menjadi 와서 (오 + 아서).

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'It rained, so I stayed home.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Karena hujan, saya ada di rumah.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use rain subject (비가) + come cause (와서) + home at (집에) + stayed (있었어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan subjek hujan (비가) + datang sebab (와서) + di rumah (집에) + ada lampau (있었어요).

meaningEn: Reason/cause connective suitable for commands, suggestions, and subjective reasons.
meaningId: Penhubung alasan/sebab yang cocok untuk kalimat perintah, ajakan, dan alasan subjektif.

notesEn.usage: Provides a reason/justification, especially before imperative (~세요) or propositional (~갑시다 / ~까요) endings.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar berakhiran Vokal -> ~니까 / Kata Dasar berakhiran Konsonan -> ~으니까.
notesId.usage: Memberikan alasan/justifikasi, terutama sebelum akhiran perintah (~세요) atau ajakan (~갑시다 / ~까요).
notesId.nuance: Penekanan subjektif yang lebih kuat daripada ~아서/어서/해서.

examples.meaningEn: Since the weather is nice, let's go out.
examples.meaningId: Karena cuacanya bagus, mari kita keluar.

examples.meaningEn: Since I am busy, please come tomorrow.
examples.meaningId: Karena saya sibuk, silakan datang besok.

examples.meaningEn: Since it is raining, use an umbrella.

quiz.question: Which causal connector is required when the second clause is an imperative command (~세요)?
quiz.explanationEn: ~(으)니까 must be used instead of ~아서/어서 when following up with imperative commands or suggestions.
quiz.explanationId: ~(으)니까 harus digunakan daripada ~아서/어서 jika diikuti oleh kalimat perintah atau ajakan.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Since it is raining, use an umbrella. -> 비가 오___ 우산을 쓰세요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 오 ends in a vowel, so attach ~니까.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Since it is raining, use an umbrella.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Karena hujan turun, gunakan payung.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use rain subject (비가) + rain comes cause (오니까) + umbrella (우산을) + use imperative (쓰세요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan subjek hujan (비가) + datang sebab (오니까) + payung (우산을) + gunakan perintah (쓰세요).

meaningEn: Background information clause ('..., so / and / but').
meaningId: Klausa informasi latar belakang ('..., jadi / dan / tetapi').

notesEn.usage: Provides context/background before making a request, proposal, or main statement.
notesEn.nuance: Softens the sentence and sets up the listener for context before delivering main content.

notesId.formation: Kata kerja -> ~는데. Kata sifat -> ~은데 (konsonan) / ~ㄴ데 (vokal). Kata benda -> ~인데.
notesId.usage: Memberikan konteks/latar belakang sebelum membuat permintaan, usulan, atau penyataan utama.
notesId.nuance: Melembutkan kalimat dan mempersiapkan pendengar dengan konteks sebelum menyampaikan isi utama.

examples.meaningEn: I am busy now, so let's talk later.
examples.meaningId: Saya sedang sibuk sekarang, jadi mari bicara nanti.

examples.meaningEn: It's raining, do you have an umbrella?
examples.meaningId: Sedang hujan, apakah kamu punya payung?

examples.meaningEn: I am studying Korean, and/but it's difficult.
examples.meaningId: Saya sedang belajar bahasa Korea, dan/tetapi rasanya sulit.

quiz.question: What is the correct background connective form for the adjective '바쁘다' (to be busy)?
quiz.explanationEn: 바쁘다 is an adjective ending in a vowel, so attach ~ㄴ데 -> 바쁜데.
quiz.explanationId: 바쁘다 adalah kata sifat berakhiran vokal, jadi tempelkan ~ㄴ데 -> 바쁜데.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: It's raining, do you have an umbrella? -> 비가 오___ 우산이 있어요?
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: 오다 is an active verb, so attach ~는데.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: 오다 adalah kata kerja aktif, jadi tempelkan ~는데.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I am busy now, so let's talk later.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya sedang sibuk sekarang, jadi mari bicara nanti.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use now (지금) + busy context (바쁜데) + later (나중에) + talk (이야기해요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan sekarang (지금) + konteks sibuk (바쁜데) + nanti (나중에) + berbicara (이야기해요).
